methods.label: Use the diameter and the side ratio
methods.explanation:
Interpret “inscribed” in the sense illustrated: the circle is tangent to the rectangle's two long sides.

[Figure 1](figures/2012_AMC_12B_Q02_question_fig1.svg)

The distance between those sides is the circle's diameter, so the rectangle's width is \(2\cdot5=10\). The length-to-width ratio is \(2:1\), so its length is \(2\cdot10=20\). Its area is therefore
\[
20\cdot10=\boxed{200}.
\]
Strictly, an inscribed circle touches all four sides. That would make both rectangle dimensions equal to the diameter \(10\), contradicting the given \(2:1\) ratio. Thus the illustrated interpretation gives \(\boxed{200}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\); the strict interpretation has no such rectangle.
methods.levelReason: The calculation needs only diameter equals twice radius, a simple ratio, and length times width.

limitations: The word “inscribed” is used loosely in the displayed item. The numerical answer relies on the two tangencies shown, rather than tangency to all four sides.
